arxiv-2006-08820.creator: Fernando Santos, Ingrid Nunes, Ana L. C. Bazzan
arxiv-2006-08820.description: Abstract The agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) paradigm has been used to analyze, reproduce, and predict phenomena related to many application areas. Although there are many agent-based platforms that support simulation development, they rely on programming languages that require extensive programming knowledge.

arxiv-2102-06953.title: Time-fractional kinetic equation for the non-Markovian kinetic processes
arxiv-2102-06953.creator: E. Aydiner
arxiv-2102-06953.description: Abstract In this study, we analytically formulated the path integral representation of the conditional probabilities for non-Markovian kinetic processes in terms of the free energy of the thermodynamic system. We carry out analytically the time-fractional kinetic equations for these processes. Thus, in a simple way, we generalize path integral solutions of the Markovian to the non-Markovian cases.

arxiv-2112-15411.title: Disjoint Contrastive Regression Learning for Multi-Sourced Annotations
arxiv-2112-15411.creator: Xiaoqian Ruan, Gaoang Wang
arxiv-2112-15411.description: Abstract Large-scale datasets are important for the development of deep learning models. Such datasets usually require a heavy workload of annotations, which are extremely time-consuming and expensive. To accelerate the annotation procedure, multiple annotators may be employed to label different subsets of the data.

arxiv-2402-16953.title: Exploring the Sensitivity to Non-Standard Neutrino Interactions of NaI and Cryogenic CsI Detectors at the Spallation Neutron Source

arxiv-2402-16953.description: Abstract After the first observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE ν \nu NS) by the COHERENT collaboration, many efforts are being made to improve the measurement of this process, making it possible to constrain new physics in the neutrino sector.

arxiv-2507-13442.title: Reconstructing galactic feedback history via the Lyman- α \alpha forest with Habitable Worlds Observatory
arxiv-2507-13442.creator: Megan T. Tillman, Joseph N. Burchett, Blakesley Burkhart, Vikram Khaire, Sanchayeeta Borthakur
arxiv-2507-13442.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Megan T. Tillman, Joseph N. Burchett, Blakesley Burkhart, Vikram Khaire, Sanchayeeta Borthakur. Recent studies have focused on the low- z z Ly α \alpha forest as a potential constraint on galactic feedback, as different AGN and stellar feedback models in hydrodynamic simulations produce varying intergalactic medium (IGM) statistics. However, existing low- z z Ly α \alpha forest data provide insufficient observational constraints for simulations due to their low precision and the lack of observations from z ∼ 0.4 z\sim 0.4 to 1.8 1.8 .

arxiv-2508-15586.title: Eigen-Portfolios: From Single-Component Models to Ensemble Approaches
arxiv-2508-15586.creator: Zhengxiang Zhou, Yuqi Luan
arxiv-2508-15586.description: Abstract The increasing integration of data science techniques into quantitative finance has enabled more systematic and data-driven approaches to portfolio construction. This paper investigates the use of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in constructing eigen-portfolios—portfolios derived from the principal components of the asset return correlation matrix.

arxiv-2601-02953.title: Spectral and Phase Structure of a QCD-Inspired Unitary Matrix Model with Fisher-Hartwig Singularities
arxiv-2601-02953.creator: Anuj Malik, Anees Ahmed
arxiv-2601-02953.description: Abstract We investigate the large N N limit of a complex action unitary matrix model with Fisher-Hartwig singularities, motivated by QCD-inspired models with complexified potentials. We show that the model exhibits multiple ungapped phases and a single gapped phase. The phases are characterized by Fisher-Hartwig singularities in the complex plane.

arxiv-2602-15855.title: Kalman-Inspired Runtime Stability and Recovery in Hybrid Reasoning Systems
arxiv-2602-15855.creator: Barak Or
arxiv-2602-15855.description: Abstract Hybrid reasoning systems that combine learned components with model-based inference are increasingly deployed in tool-augmented decision loops, yet their runtime behavior under partial observability and sustained evidence mismatch remains poorly understood. In practice, failures often arise as gradual divergence of internal reasoning dynamics rather than as isolated prediction errors.

pmc-11337745.title: Factors affecting COVID-19 vaccine uptake in populations with higher education: insights from a cross-sectional study among university students in Malawi
pmc-11337745.creator: Qebo Kornelio Madhlopa, Matthews Mtumbuka, Joel Kumwenda, Thomas Arron Illingworth, Marie-Claire Van Hout, Joseph Mfutso-Bengo, Chomora Mikeka, Isaac Thom Shawa
pmc-11337745.description: BackgroundThe Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) vaccines were rolled out in many countries; however, sub-optimal COVID-19 vaccine uptake remains a major public health concern globally. This study aimed at assessing the factors that affected the uptake, hesitancy, and resistance of the COVID-19 vaccine among university undergraduate students in Malawi, a least developed country in Africa.

pmc-11409406.title: Rib fractures – Patient education series: understanding trauma and emergency surgery conditions
pmc-11409406.creator: Joshua Dilday, Elliott R Haut
pmc-11409406.description: nough force is applied to them. Rib fractures can be a common painful ailment after any trauma. Although they are more likely to occur from blunt trauma (eg, falls or motor vehicle crashes), they can also be caused by penetrating traumatic injuries (eg, gunshots or stabbings), sports injuries, and even coughing. The severity of rib fractures spans a large spectrum.

pmc-11516540.title: A Process Evaluation in a Randomized Controlled Trial among Adults with Acetabular Dysplasia
pmc-11516540.creator: J S Jacobsen, R Evans, K Morgan, K Thorborg, L G Oestergaard, D Sørensen
pmc-11516540.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe 2021 framework from the UK’s Medical Research Council defines evaluation as a theory-driven approach to examine how well an intervention works. However, the application of these guidelines can be challenging. Therefore, using a process evaluation case study on an exercise and patient education intervention for adults with acetabular dysplasia, we reflect on which specific aspects were relevant for the evaluation of the intervention and why.

pmc-11545900.title: Multimorbidity and Multiple Disabilities: Present Status and the Roles of Rehabilitation
pmc-11545900.creator: Masahiro Kohzuki, Francesco Giallauria
pmc-11545900.description: The world is aging, and an increasing number of countries are becoming aged or super-aged societies. Japan has already become the world’s first super-aged society, with an aging rate of 29.1% of the entire population of the country. As of 15 September 2021, there were approximately 36.40 million people aged 65 years and over.

pmc-11715774.title: Cognitive training related changes in fMRI activations: a neural mechanism of transfer to executive functions in normal aging
pmc-11715774.creator: Paulina Skolasinska, Shuo Qin, Hyun Kyu Lee, Michelle W Voss, Chandramallika Basak
pmc-11715774.description: BackgroundImprovement of cognitive functions is often accompanied by changes in brain function after cognitive training in older adults. In this large‐scale dual‐site fMRI study we investigated the effects of BrainHQ cognitive training (CT; ®Posit Science Inc.) and an active control (AC) group on brain activations during a demanding executive control (EC) task among cognitively normal older adults.

pmc-12578918.title: Crustal constraints on the surface expression of mantle upwelling in a back-arc passive margin setting

pmc-12726829.title: DendroTweaks, an interactive approach for unraveling dendritic dynamics
pmc-12726829.creator: Roman Makarov, Spyridon Chavlis, Panayiota Poirazi, Casey M Schneider-Mizell, Roman Makarov, Spyridon Chavlis, Panayiota Poirazi
pmc-12726829.description: Neurons rely on the interplay between two critical components, dendritic morphology and ion channels, to transform synaptic inputs into a sequence of somatic spikes. Detailed biophysical models with active dendrites have been instrumental in exploring this interaction. However, such models can be challenging to understand and validate due to the large number of parameters involved.

pmc-12805478.title: Impact of Real-Time Multiplex PCR Testing for Respiratory Viruses on Antibiotic Use
pmc-12805478.creator: Zeynep Tekin-Taş, Hasan Selçuk Özger, Fidan Sultanova, Merve Büyükkörük, Gülendam Bozdayı, Kayhan Çağlar, Özlem Güzel Tunçcan, Murat Dizbay
pmc-12805478.description: ObjectiveReal-time multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test increases the detection of viral respiratory tract infections. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of real-time multiplex PCR on antibiotic use in viral respiratory tract infections. Materials and MethodsThis retrospective study included patients who underwent respiratory multiplex PCR tests. Patients were grouped into influenza-like illness, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and co-infection.
